mainEntity.name: Does the calculator check my Roth IRA contribution eligibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It models a hypothetical amount. Income phaseouts, compensation, filing status, other IRA contributions, and future-year rules are not calculated.

mainEntity.name: Why does it add the contribution after growth?

acceptedAnswer.text: The example assumes each year's contribution arrives at year-end. Contributions made earlier may have more time to grow, so a different contribution schedule would produce another result.

mainEntity.name: Is this the same as a Roth conversion calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A conversion moves money from an existing account and can create a tax bill. This estimate models a current Roth IRA balance plus hypothetical new annual contributions, without conversion taxes.

mainEntity.name: How do I tell contributions from modeled growth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Record the starting balance plus every hypothetical annual contribution separately. Subtract that total from the illustrative ending balance to identify modeled growth. The worksheet scenarios make this distinction explicit; neither amount is guaranteed.

mainEntity.name: Does a zero-return scenario show the worst possible outcome?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It checks that the model returns the starting balance plus contributions when no growth is assumed. Negative returns can produce smaller results, and this constant-rate calculator does not reproduce changing real-world returns.
